facts.text: Olin began in 1835 as Elkford, later Walnut Fork, then Rome in 1842, and was renamed Olin in 1868 after railroad superintendent D.A.
The Wapsipinicon River borders Olin to the east, draining the surrounding watershed and occasionally flooding low‑lying areas during heavy rains.
For decades, the rhythmic whistles of the Paul and Pacific trains echoed through Olin’s streets until the 1970s, when the line was abandoned.
Today, Olin’s residents celebrate their heritage at the annual Olin Jamboree, a gathering that showcases rural charm and community spirit.
